title: The Parser's Tongue
tagline: turn what the player typed into what the game does
hints: `size_t space = line.find(' ');` gives you the position of the first space, or `std::string::npos` when there is none.
When there IS no space the whole line is the verb and the rest is empty. When there is one: `verb = line.substr(0, space);` and `rest = line.substr(space + 1);`
`substr(start)` runs to the end of the string. `substr(start, count)` takes count characters. Getting these two mixed up is most of what goes wrong with strings.
Order your checks: empty line first, then look, then go, then take, then the catch-all. And test the `rest.empty()` case inside go and take before using it.
The loop is `while (std::getline(std::cin, line))`, with `if (line == "quit") break;` as the first thing inside.
